Scroll to watch a Kia get built, station by station — the same sequence that happens on the floor in West Point, Georgia.

Scroll
01STAMP
02WELD

05QUALITY

Uncoiled. Cut. Pressed into shape.

Steel coils are unrolled, sheared to size, and carried through four press stations, each shaping the panel further under thousands of tons of force.

Panels, welded into one shell.

Robotic arms bring individually stamped panels together and weld them into a single rigid body-in-white structure.

Paint, from bare metal to color.

Multi-stage coating lines apply primer, color, and clearcoat in a controlled, dust-free environment.

Engine, wheels, trim — installed.

Chassis, powertrain, and interior components come together on the general assembly line, station by station.

Checked. Then it drives off the line.

Every unit passes more than 60 quality checks before it ever leaves West Point, Georgia.

West Point, Georgia · Est. 2006

The road to West Point.

From a groundbreaking in the red clay to five million vehicles built by hand and by robot — the story of Kia's flagship U.S. plant.

Click a milestone to see the story.

October 2006

Breaking ground

With America's first Kia groundbreaking ceremony, Kia takes its first step into the state of Georgia.

2006 – 2009

Rising from red clay

Construction of the West Point, Georgia plant ran for three years, beginning in 2006.

November 2009

Start of production

The moment Kia Georgia's first vehicle rolled off the line.

July 2013

One million vehicles

After moving from one to two, then three shifts starting in 2009, Kia Georgia reached one million vehicles built in record time.

September 2019

Three million vehicles

Led by the Telluride, in production since 2019, Kia Georgia reaches three million vehicles built.

March 2021

A new brand identity

Kia launches a new brand logo, reborn with a new identity and a new brand.

June 2025

First EV, fully charged

Kia Georgia begins production of the EV9, the state's first electric vehicle, preparing for the future of mobility.

December 2025

IONNA comes online

Kia and IONNA partner to install an EV charging station on campus, strengthening Georgia's EV ecosystem.

January 2026

Ringing in the New Year

Kia celebrates the launch of the all-new Telluride, built exclusively for North America, with the Times Square New Year's Eve countdown.

January 2026

Solar canopy complete

Kia Georgia partners with Georgia Power to install a solar canopy, generating clean energy on-site.

February 2026

Five million vehicles

Kia Georgia reaches five million vehicles built while adding hybrid to its lineup — reborn as a flexible plant capable of producing ICE, EV, and hybrid vehicles alike.
